payload.supporting_quote: Serum levels of 25(OH)D were determined significantly lower in migraine patients (n=952) in comparison with healthy controls (n=8013) [eight studies, PQ<0.1, I2=94%, RE model MD=-4.11, 95% CI=(-6.48, -1.74)].
Migraine patients had significantly lower mean (SD) of serum VitD (30 (16) ng/mL) than healthy subjects (43 (19) ng/mL) (P < .001).
There was no significant difference in 25(OH)D concentration between cases and controls.
There was no significant difference among the patients with cluster headache, migraineurs, and controls.
Compared with controls, mean 25(OH)D concentration was significantly lower in patients with arthritis ... but not in patients with headache or migraine (MD: -2·53 nmol/l; P=0·06).
